item.title: “Poetry Can Be Conceived as an Art of Disruption”: A Conversation with Gisela Heffes, by Claudia Cavallin
East Coast Book Tour to Promote World Literature Today Centennial Anthology
item.description: The week of March 23–27, Daniel Simon will do a series of East Coast events to promote A Compass on the Navigable Sea: 100 Years of World Literature (2026), his edited anthology commemorating the WLT centennial.

item.title: Stubbornly Analog, by Rob Vollmar
item.description: WLT book review editor Rob Vollmar examines the renaissance of dungeon synth among tape collectors betting (and winning) on a postcapitalist future.

item.title: Why Does the Ocean Appear Motionless from an Airplane?, by Zsuzsa Selyem
item.description: A fiction excerpt by Zsuzsa Selyem, translated from the Hungarian, from a novel that follows a handful of people across a small cosmos of pre- and post-1989 East Europe.

item.title: The Dancers and the Dance: David Rigsbee’s Watchman in the Knife Factory, by Tim Hunt
item.description: Tim Hunt reviews David Rigsbee’s 2024 collection of poems.

item.title: The God of the Donated Clothes Magazine, by Admir Skodo
item.description: Years after spending three weeks in a refugee camp in Sweden, a Bosnian police detective learns the true identity of the camp’s gatekeeper of clothing.

item.title: WLT Podcast
item.description: Go beyond the pages of WLT in the World Literature Today podcast, hosted by Sonja Srinivasan. Sonja speaks with contributors and highlights several reviews, contributors read from their work, and you can test your knowledge with a few trivia questions. You'll also find out what's happening at WLT beyond the magazine.

item.title: Irrefutably Human: Dearness as Both Cost and Affect in the Poetry of Shanta Acharya, by Shyamasri Maji
item.description: Shyamasri Maji reviews Dear Life, Shanta Acharya’s 2025 collection of poems.

item.title: Creating Infinite Universes with Language: A Conversation with Zimbabwean Cultural Activist, Writer, and Performance Poet Cynthia Marangwanda, by Mbizo Chirasha
item.description: Mbizo Chirasha interviews Zimbabwean cultural activist, writer, and performance poet Cynthia Marangwanda.
